quests.hint: Formally giving up a claim, right, or title, often for someone else's benefit.
quests.explanation: 'Renounce a claim' is the go-to phrase. It can also mean giving up a habit or belief — 'to renounce violence.'
quests.textToSpeak: She decided to ___ her claim to the family business in favor of her brother.
quests.correctAnswer: She decided to renounce her claim to the family business in favor of her brother.

quests.hint: Given with complete enthusiasm and zero hesitation.
quests.explanation: Wholehearted is one word. 'Wholehearted support' means total commitment, without any doubts held back.
quests.textToSpeak: He gave the plan his ___ support from the very first meeting.
quests.correctAnswer: He gave the plan his wholehearted support from the very first meeting.

quests.hint: Doubts or concerns that make you hesitant, even if you go along with something anyway.
quests.explanation: 'Have reservations about' is the one that sounds most natural. It's almost always used in the plural, even for one specific worry.
quests.textToSpeak: I have some ___ about the new schedule, but I'm willing to give it a try.
quests.correctAnswer: I have some reservations about the new schedule, but I'm willing to give it a try.

quests.hint: The power to block a decision, even if everyone else has agreed to it.
quests.explanation: 'The power to veto' works as a noun here; 'to veto a decision' uses it as a verb — either way, blocking something outright.
quests.textToSpeak: As the majority shareholder, he had the power to ___ any decision the board made.
quests.correctAnswer: As the majority shareholder, he had the power to veto any decision the board made.

quests.hint: Passing a task on to someone else instead of doing it all yourself.
quests.explanation: 'Delegate tasks' is essential management advice. As a noun, 'a delegate' means a representative sent to a meeting, in a different context.
quests.textToSpeak: A good manager knows when to ___ tasks instead of doing everything herself.
quests.correctAnswer: A good manager knows when to delegate tasks instead of doing everything herself.

quests.hint: Formally agreeing to take on a task or responsibility.
quests.explanation: 'Undertake a project' is a more formal way of saying 'take on.' The noun form is 'undertaking' — 'a serious undertaking.'
quests.textToSpeak: She agreed to ___ the project with the proviso that adequate funding would be made available.
quests.correctAnswer: She agreed to undertake the project with the proviso that adequate funding would be made available.

quests.hint: A small but important condition attached to an otherwise simple agreement.
quests.explanation: 'With one caveat' is a common phrase for adding a condition to your agreement. It comes from Latin, meaning 'let him beware.'
quests.textToSpeak: I'll agree to help, with one ___: I need to leave by six.
quests.correctAnswer: I'll agree to help, with one caveat: I need to leave by six.

quests.hint: Clear personal limits that protect your time, energy, or wellbeing.
quests.explanation: 'Set boundaries' is common modern advice for a healthy work-life balance. It's almost always used in the plural.
quests.textToSpeak: Setting clear ___ at work helped her avoid burnout.
quests.correctAnswer: Setting clear boundaries at work helped her avoid burnout.

quests.hint: Understood by everyone involved, even though nobody actually says it out loud.
quests.explanation: 'An unspoken agreement' is one everyone follows without ever discussing it directly, closely related to 'tacit.'
quests.textToSpeak: There was an ___ agreement that nobody would mention the mistake again.
quests.correctAnswer: There was an unspoken agreement that nobody would mention the mistake again.

quests.hint: Officially taking back a statement you previously made.
quests.explanation: 'Ordered to retract' a story is common in journalism after an error. The noun form is 'retraction.'
quests.textToSpeak: The newspaper was ordered to ___ the story and publish a front-page correction.
quests.correctAnswer: The newspaper was ordered to retract the story and publish a front-page correction.

quests.hint: A statement made to limit legal responsibility or clarify that something isn't guaranteed.
quests.explanation: 'Publish a disclaimer' is the phrase to remember. It's a noun, so it always needs an article — 'a disclaimer,' never simply 'disclaimer.'
quests.textToSpeak: The company published a ___ stating that its earlier announcement had contained inaccurate figures.
quests.correctAnswer: The company published a disclaimer stating that its earlier announcement had contained inaccurate figures.

quests.hint: Publicly stating you don't support or agree with something someone else said or did.
quests.explanation: 'Quickly disavowed' shows a fast, deliberate distancing from a comment. The base form is 'disavow' — 'to disavow a statement.'
quests.textToSpeak: The spokesperson quickly ___ the comments made by a company colleague at the conference.
quests.correctAnswer: The spokesperson quickly disavowed the comments made by a company colleague at the conference.

quests.hint: The process of passing responsibility from one person to their replacement.
quests.explanation: Handover is one word as a noun. As two words, 'hand over' becomes the verb — 'she handed over the keys.'
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ between the outgoing and incoming manager took almost a full week.
quests.correctAnswer: The handover between the outgoing and incoming manager took almost a full week.

quests.hint: Giving up control of something you've held for a long time, often reluctantly.
quests.explanation: 'Relinquish control' is a formal, weighty word for letting go, suggesting real difficulty in finally releasing something.
quests.textToSpeak: After thirty years, she was finally ready to ___ control of the company she'd built.
quests.correctAnswer: After thirty years, she was finally ready to relinquish control of the company she'd built.

quests.hint: The person who takes over a role after someone else leaves it.
quests.explanation: 'Name a successor' is common when planning a leadership transition. The verb form is 'succeed' — 'to succeed someone in a role.'
quests.textToSpeak: The board still hadn't named a ___ by the time the CEO announced her retirement.
quests.correctAnswer: The board still hadn't named a successor by the time the CEO announced her retirement.

quests.hint: A final payment given to an employee when their job ends.
quests.explanation: 'Severance package' is the standard phrase, from 'sever,' meaning to cut off or separate.
quests.textToSpeak: The company offered a generous ___ package to everyone affected by the closure.
quests.correctAnswer: The company offered a generous severance package to everyone affected by the closure.

quests.hint: A formal complaint raised by an employee about unfair treatment.
quests.explanation: 'File a grievance' is standard HR language, more formal and official than simply 'a complaint.'
quests.textToSpeak: Several staff members filed a formal ___ over the change in working hours.
quests.correctAnswer: Several staff members filed a formal grievance over the change in working hours.

quests.hint: The negative consequences that follow a scandal or crisis, often lasting a long time.
quests.explanation: 'The fallout from' something describes lasting damage after an event, originally radioactive particles settling after an explosion.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ from the scandal cost the company several major clients.
quests.correctAnswer: The fallout from the scandal cost the company several major clients.

quests.hint: A final judgment or opinion reached after carefully weighing everything.
quests.explanation: 'The audience's verdict' uses the word more broadly than just in court — any considered final opinion counts.
quests.textToSpeak: Critics were divided, but the audience's ___ was overwhelmingly positive.
quests.correctAnswer: Critics were divided, but the audience's verdict was overwhelmingly positive.

quests.hint: A plan going badly wrong, causing the exact opposite of what was intended.
quests.explanation: 'Completely backfire' is a vivid phrase, originally describing a gun firing backward instead of forward.
quests.textToSpeak: The plan to cut costs by reducing staff was about to completely ___.
quests.correctAnswer: The plan to cut costs by reducing staff was about to completely backfire.

quests.hint: The satisfying feeling of finally being proven right after facing doubt or criticism.
quests.explanation: 'Total vindication' is a strong, satisfying feeling. The verb form is 'vindicate' — 'to vindicate someone's decision.'
quests.textToSpeak: Winning the award felt like total ___ after years of being doubted.
quests.correctAnswer: Winning the award felt like total vindication after years of being doubted.

quests.hint: A moment when past mistakes finally catch up and must be faced.
quests.explanation: 'A reckoning for' something describes consequences finally arriving after being avoided for a long time.
quests.textToSpeak: The financial crisis brought a ___ for the reckless lending practices of the previous decade.
quests.correctAnswer: The financial crisis brought a reckoning for the reckless lending practices of the previous decade.

quests.hint: The question of whether something is genuinely right or wrong.
quests.explanation: 'Questions about the morality of' a decision are common in ethical debates. The adjective form is 'moral' — 'a moral dilemma.'
quests.textToSpeak: The decision raised serious questions about the ___ of prioritising profit over human welfare.
quests.correctAnswer: The decision raised serious questions about the morality of prioritising profit over human welfare.

quests.hint: Completely honest and direct, with nothing softened or dressed up.
quests.explanation: 'An unvarnished assessment' tells you the truth plainly, from the idea of wood left bare, without a polished coating.
quests.textToSpeak: She appreciated his ___ assessment of the situation, however uncomfortable it was to hear.
quests.correctAnswer: She appreciated his unvarnished assessment of the situation, however uncomfortable it was to hear.

quests.hint: An introduction that sets out the values or purpose behind what follows.
quests.explanation: 'The preamble to' a speech or document lays the groundwork before the main content begins, from Latin for 'to walk before.'
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ to her speech laid out the values that would guide everything she said next.
quests.correctAnswer: The preamble to her speech laid out the values that would guide everything she said next.

quests.hint: The commonly accepted view within a field, rarely questioned by most people.
quests.explanation: 'Challenge the prevailing orthodoxy' means pushing back against accepted wisdom. Its opposite is being 'unorthodox.'
quests.textToSpeak: The paper directly challenged the prevailing ___ on how language is acquired in early childhood.
quests.correctAnswer: The paper directly challenged the prevailing orthodoxy on how language is acquired in early childhood.

quests.hint: A shared way of thinking that shapes how a group of people generally behaves.
quests.explanation: 'Shift the public mentality' describes changing widely held attitudes. 'A winning mentality' is common in sport, in a different context.
quests.textToSpeak: Shifting the public ___ around mental health requires sustained effort over many years.
quests.correctAnswer: Shifting the public mentality around mental health requires sustained effort over many years.

quests.hint: The core, defining quality that something really comes down to.
quests.explanation: 'At its essence' introduces the simplest, truest description of something complex. The adjective form is 'essential.'
quests.textToSpeak: At its ___, great leadership is simply the art of helping others do their very best work.
quests.correctAnswer: At its essence, great leadership is simply the art of helping others do their very best work.

quests.hint: The very highest point of success someone can reach in their field.
quests.explanation: 'The absolute pinnacle of' a career is the highest possible achievement. It literally means the peak of a mountain.
quests.textToSpeak: She reached the absolute ___ of her profession when she was appointed to the international court.
quests.correctAnswer: She reached the absolute pinnacle of her profession when she was appointed to the international court.

quests.hint: The final, crowning result of years of sustained effort.
quests.explanation: 'The culmination of' decades of work is the moment everything finally comes together. The verb form is 'culminate.'
quests.textToSpeak: Her final lecture was the ___ of forty years of research, teaching, and passionate advocacy.
quests.correctAnswer: Her final lecture was the culmination of forty years of research, teaching, and passionate advocacy.
